newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Islamist faces 54 years for newspaper attack.
newsitem.headline: Turk Islamist faces 54 years for newspaper attack.

text.p: A Turkish Islamist student went on trial on Thursday facing up to 54 years in jail for allegedly carrying out an armed attack on the headquarters of a major secularist newspaper.

"The prosecutor's indictment asks that Huseyin Vuran be sentenced to up to 30 years in jail for armed attack and another 24 years maximum for threatening and wounding people by using a gun," Anatolian news agency said.
Vural is accused of shooting and injuring two employees of the daily Hurriyet in an attack on the paper's main building in Istanbul in May.
No formal plea is needed under Turkish law. Vuran's lawyer told the court that his client had taken leave from studying the Moslem religion at university because of mental illness.
The court indictment said that Vuran attacked the newspaper because it had offended his beliefs.
A separate court began hearing a case against another leading secularist daily newspaper that faces closure for interviewing an alleged member of an armed Islamist group.

Istanbul state security court put on trial the owner, an editor and a correspondent of the liberal daily Yeni Yuzyil for allegedly promoting the Great Islamic Eastern Raiders - Front (IBDA-C) group in the March interview.

They are also charged with "spreading separatism and inciting hatred" because of the article and face three years in jail plus the closure of the paper. The alleged IBDA-C member, Hayrettin Soykan, faces the same charges.
Soykan, who is also the editor of an Islamic magazine, was the only accused to appear in court.
He denied membership of the group and said the newspaper had distorted his comments in the interview, headlined, "Islamists Take Up Arms".
Yeni Yuzyil's owner Dinc Bilgin is one of the country's leading press barons.

He owns the influential Sabah Media group, part of the maintream secularist media that harshly cricticised former Islamist prime minister Necmettin Erbakan for his attempts to alter Turkey's secularist system.
Erbakan left office last week under intense pressure from the secularist elite after a stormy year as the secularist country's first Islamist leader.
